narrative:
The model estimated a 56.9% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because that is above the failure threshold used for this decision, your law school application was denied.

The strongest factor was your part-time enrollment status: most accepted students were full-time (92.8%), and being part-time pushed the prediction toward failure more than any other factor. The second strongest was your third-year class standing. You were in the third decile, compared with an average of about the sixth decile among accepted students; that lower standing also pushed toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 2.70, below the accepted average of 3.23, was the third most influential factor. In this prediction, it pushed slightly toward passing rather than failure, but it was not strong enough to outweigh the two factors above.

To strengthen a future application, focus on demonstrable academic improvement and bar-exam readiness: consider full-time study if possible, consult your school about raising your class standing or addressing its causes, and seek advising on LSAT preparation and a structured bar-preparation plan. You may also ask admissions for feedback and consider explaining any circumstances behind your grades.
